$~$

The overall purpose of this project is to identify if there are predilections for certain germline p53 mutations in certain tissues due to similar developmental origins, which can then potentially influence specific epigenomic landscapes in these tissues. As germline p53 mutations would be present in all cells from conception, they would be carried through all developmental tissues and their organ derivatives, and thus could shape the unique epigenetics specific to tissues. Consequently, these enrichments of mutations could favor carcinogenesis in specific tissues. 

$~$

$~$

This code calls all the packages used in this document's analysis, and sets a seed for reproducibility. I also introduce a function to add significance stars to p-values generated by summary tables later on.

$~$


``` r
#load (and install if needed) pacman and use it to load important packages
if (!require("pacman", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pacman"); library(pacman)
pacman::p_load(BiocManager, stringr, dplyr, tidyverse, ggplot2, kableExtra, knitr, devtools, rmarkdown, readr, readxl, patchwork, data.table, scales, grid, gridExtra, condformat, cowplot, janitor, pivottabler, reshape2, tibble, gtools, ggpubr, ggrepel, RColorBrewer, ComplexHeatmap, bookdown, ggalluvial, gt, gtsummary, webshot2, dendextend, factoextra, NbClust, fpc, cluster, fossil, nnet, MASS, survminer, survival, ggh4x, corrplot, ggstats, car, caret, venn, broom.helpers)

#update all loaded packages
#pacman::p_update() 

#set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(1212)

# create function to show significance stars in gt summary tables 
pvalue_with_stars <- function(x) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    x < 0.001 ~ paste0(style_pvalue(x, digits = 3), " (***)"),
    x < 0.01 ~ paste0(style_pvalue(x, digits = 3), " (**)"),
    x < 0.05 ~ paste0(style_pvalue(x, digits = 3), " (*)"),
    TRUE ~ style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)
  )
}

# create function to pivot wider multinomial gt summary tables
multinom_pivot_wider <- function(x) {
  # check inputs match expectatations
  if (!inherits(x, "tbl_regression") || !inherits(x$model_obj, "multinom")) {
    stop("`x=` must be class 'tbl_regression' summary of a `nnet::multinom()` model.")
  }
  
  # create tibble of results
  df <- tibble::tibble(outcome_level = unique(x$table_body$groupname_col))
  df$tbl <- 
    purrr::map(
      df$outcome_level,
      function(lvl) {
        gtsummary::modify_table_body(
          x, 
          ~dplyr::filter(.x, .data$groupname_col %in% lvl) %>%
            dplyr::ungroup() %>%
            dplyr::select(-.data$groupname_col)
        )
      }
    )
  
  tbl_merge(df$tbl, tab_spanner = paste0("**", df$outcome_level, "**"))
}

# create function to put n numbers and other stats above plots
stat_box_data <- function(y) {
  return( 
    data.frame(
      y = 1.35 + 1.1 * max(y), 
      label = paste('n =', length(y), '\n'
                    #,
                    #'mean =', round(mean(y), 2), "\n"
                    ,
                    "median =", round(median(y), 2), "\n"
                    )
    )
  )
}

# set theme for gtsummary tables before making plots, compact reduces font size and cell padding
theme_gtsummary_compact(font_size = 15) # default is 13 for gt tables and 8 for all other output types
```

# **Input Data** {#inputdata}

$~$

First I downloaded the entire germline variant dataset from the TP53 Database [@tp53database2022], downloaded from this site: <https://tp53.cancer.gov/view_data?bq_view_name=GermlineDownload>. To get to this page, go to <https://tp53.cancer.gov/> --\> Germline Variants --\> Data Downloads Germline Variants --\> TP53 germline variants and family history (data file) --\> click Preview icon to get to filterable data table --\> download entire table without any filters.

$~$

I also took p53 mutations described in Figure 7J of @chen2021 as being transcriptionally rescued after the administration of arsenic trioxide (ATO) i.e. all mutations with more than 2-fold change of transcriptional activity (upper right and lower right quadrants). ATO has been proposed as a possible therapeutic agent for Li-Fraumeni Syndrome where short doses could prevent cancer incidence [@Pantziarka2022]. So it would be good to track which mutations in the TP53 database germline mutant dataset could potentially be rescued by this agent.

$~$

I also downloaded information for all p53 mutants tested for ATO rescue from <http://www.rescuep53.net/explore.html> and took Supplementary Table S6 from @song2023. The site was created from the results of this paper and Supplementary Table S6 specifically lists which mutations are type 1, 2a (both of which had notable ATO-mediated rescue), 2b, or 3 mutants (either less effectively rescued or not rescued at all after ATO). To get mutations from the website, I went to <http://www.rescuep53.net/explore.html>, changed the upper left dropdown to show all 800 mutations, and manually copied and pasted all the columns' information into an Excel file, which I have then read in below.

$~$

I also took p53 mutations described in Figure 5C of @tang2022 as being transcriptionally rescued after the administration of potassium antimony tartrate (PAT).

$~$

In this code, I have then read in all items.

$~$



# **Cleaning Input Data** {#cleaningdata}

$~$

Next, I cleaned the data by removing entries with nondescript cancers, clarifying mutations without specific residues, improving mutation formatting, only keeping entries of confirmed germline carriers, removing a mutation documented as a founder effect, collapsing similar category cancers into one cancer type, compiling ages at diagnosis or follow-up into age strata, and removing mutations which have no ages or sexes listed. I am considering the short topology column for cancers because not every cancer has good detailed annotations for specific cancer types. However, for adrenal gland and bone cancers, they are primarily comprised of 1 morphology each, so I am using that morphology for subsequent calculations. I then saved this cleaned data (along with a slight modification to include certain morphologies) as its own CSV file which can be read into R again or used on its own at any time. Moreover, I split the data into patients with either 1 cancer or multiple cancers to do individual analyses, and saved them as separate CSV files.

$~$


``` r
#remove data with unknown site or other sites short topology for cancer
origdbcleaned <- origdbdistinct %>% 
  filter(!Short_topo %in% c("OTHER SITES", 
                            "UNKNOWN SITE")) %>%
  remove_rownames()

#concatenate codon number and mutation type to "p.?" mutations which have unspecified residues and rename intronic/splice mutations as such
origdbcleaned <- origdbcleaned %>% 
  mutate(ProtDescription = ifelse(ProtDescription %in% c("p.?"),
                                  paste(ProtDescription, 
                                        Codon_number, 
                                        Effect,
                                        sep = "-"), 
                                  ProtDescription)) %>%
  mutate(ProtDescription = gsub("\\?-0-splice|\\?-0-intronic",
                                "Intronic",
                                ProtDescription)) %>% 
  remove_rownames()

#remove "p." prefix from all mutations to clean up visually
origdbcleaned$ProtDescription <- substring(origdbcleaned$ProtDescription, 3) 

#only keep data of confirmed germline carriers
origdbcleaned <- origdbcleaned %>% 
  filter(Germline_carrier == "Confirmed") %>%
  remove_rownames()

#remove R337H data - Brazilian founder effect often removed from published papers' analyses
origdbcleaned <- origdbcleaned %>% 
  filter(ProtDescription != "R337H") %>%
  remove_rownames()

#combine BONES (other) and BONES (limbs) short topologies into 1 BONES short topology, and COLON and RECTUM, NOS short topologies into 1 COLORECTUM short topology
origdbcleaned <- origdbcleaned %>%
  mutate(Short_topo = ifelse(Short_topo %in% c('BONES (other)',
                                               'BONES (limbs)'), 
                             'BONES', 
                             Short_topo)) %>%
  mutate(Short_topo = ifelse(Short_topo %in% c("COLON",
                                               "RECTUM",
                                               "COLORECTUM, NOS"),
                             "COLORECTUM",
                             Short_topo))

#duplicate age at diagnosis column so that can add age at follow-up without disturbing original column, rearrange column order for ease in viewing, and wherever no age at diagnosis, add age at follow-up instead if it's present
origdbcleaned$Age_dx_follow <- origdbcleaned$Age_at_diagnosis
origdbcleaned <- origdbcleaned %>% 
  relocate(Age_at_diagnosis, 
           Age_dx_follow,
           .after = Age) %>%
  mutate(Age_dx_follow = ifelse(is.na(origdbcleaned$Age_dx_follow),
                                Age,
                                Age_dx_follow))

#add age stratum column ~ every 10 yrs of pts, to have at least 100 entries per stratum
origdbcleaned <- origdbcleaned %>%
  transform(Age_stratum = ifelse(Age_dx_follow <= 9,
                                 "0-9",
                                 "notyet")) %>%
  transform(Age_stratum = ifelse(Age_dx_follow >= 10 & Age_dx_follow <= 19,
                                 "10-19",
                                 Age_stratum)) %>%
  transform(Age_stratum = ifelse(Age_dx_follow >= 20 & Age_dx_follow <= 29,
                                 "20-29",
                                 Age_stratum)) %>%
  transform(Age_stratum = ifelse(Age_dx_follow >= 30 & Age_dx_follow <= 39,
                                 "30-39",
                                 Age_stratum)) %>%
  transform(Age_stratum = ifelse(Age_dx_follow >= 40,
                                 "40 and up",
                                 Age_stratum)) %>% 
  relocate(Age_stratum,
           .after = Age_dx_follow) %>% 
  drop_na(Age_stratum) %>%
  drop_na(Sex) %>% 
  distinct()

# identify pts with multiple distinct mutations and remove them, so that only have pts with 1 mut each
pts_dup_muts <- origdbcleaned %>% 
  dplyr::select(c(ProtDescription, 
                  Individual_code)) %>% 
  group_by(Individual_code) %>% 
  filter(n() > 1) %>% # first get all pts with multiple entries regardless of muts
  distinct() %>% # only keep pts with multiple entries and multiple distinct muts
  group_by(Individual_code) %>% 
  filter(n() > 1) %>% # get all pts with multiple distinct muts
  arrange(Individual_code) %>%
  pull(Individual_code) %>%
  unique()

origdbcleaned <- origdbcleaned %>%
  subset(!(Individual_code %in% pts_dup_muts)) %>%
  distinct()

# CHECK WHICH ADRENAL CANCERS ARE THERE WHICH ARE HIGHEST IN 0-9YO, ARE THEY ACC? - yes mostly ACC
# CHECK WHICH BRAIN CANCERS ARE THERE WHICH ARE HIGHEST IN 0-9YO - many types, quite a few of choroid plexus carcinoma and medulloblastoma
# CONSULT LITERATURE TO SEE IF THESE ABOVE ADRENAL AND BRAIN CANCER TYPES ARE THE MOST COMMON IN 0-9

# need to specify short topology as more detailed cancers so that results are a little more informative, 
# we already know from literature that the most common LFS tumors are bones, brain, breast, adrenal, soft tissues, 
# after looking through the data, choosing to rename adrenal and bones because most adrenal tumors are ACC and most bone tumors are osteosarcomas, 
# can make piecharts of non adrenal and bones cancers breakdown, 
# so can use express morphologies for adrenal and bones for pivot tables and subsequent calculations
# change short topologies to have express morphologies of adrenal and bones, otherwise retain original short topologies
breakdown <- origdbcleaned %>% 
  transform(Short_topo = ifelse(Short_topo %in% c("ADRENAL GLAND",
                                                  "BONES"),
                                Morphology,
                                Short_topo)) %>% 
  remove_rownames()

# to clean up formatting in short topology and morphology columns, remove NOS (not otherwise specified) and (C#._) characters
breakdown$Short_topo <- gsub(", NOS",
                             "", 
                             breakdown$Short_topo)
breakdown$Short_topo <- gsub("\\(C.*", 
                             "", 
                             breakdown$Short_topo)
breakdown$Morphology <- gsub(", NOS",
                             "", 
                             breakdown$Morphology)
breakdown$Morphology <- gsub("\\(C.*", 
                             "", 
                             breakdown$Morphology)

# combine similarly named morphologies together to collapse down and remove whitespace at beginning and end of words
breakdown <- breakdown %>% 
  transform(Morphology = ifelse(Morphology %in% c("Carcinoma"),
                                "Cancer",
                                Morphology)) %>% 
  transform(Morphology = ifelse(Morphology %in% c("Infiltrating ductular carcinoma "),
                                "Infiltrating duct carcinoma ",
                                Morphology)) %>% 
  mutate_if(is.character, 
            trimws) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  remove_rownames()

# num total families in dataset
n_distinct(breakdown$Family_code) # 1034

# find patients which have multiple cancers for individual analyses
# remove patients which didn't have cancer at follow-up and with no age of diagnosis
origdbdefcancer <- breakdown %>% 
  subset(Unaffected == FALSE) %>% 
  drop_na(Age_at_diagnosis) %>% 
  distinct()

# find patients listed once or multiple times, subset data to such patients, and compare if equivalent
ptswithcancer <- origdbdefcancer %>% 
  count(Individual_code, 
        Age_at_diagnosis, 
        Short_topo, 
        Morphology, 
        sort = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  remove_rownames()
ptswithcancer <- ptswithcancer %>% 
  count(Individual_code,
        sort = TRUE) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  remove_rownames()

solepts <- ptswithcancer %>% 
  subset(n == 1) %>% 
  remove_rownames()
solepts <- solepts[order(-solepts$n),] %>% 
  remove_rownames()
origdbsolecancer <- origdbdefcancer %>% 
  subset(origdbdefcancer$Individual_code %in% solepts$Individual_code) %>% 
  distinct()
all(origdbsolecancer$Individual_code %in% solepts$Individual_code) # should be TRUE in console

multpts <- ptswithcancer %>% 
  subset(n > 1) %>% 
  remove_rownames()
multpts <- multpts[order(-multpts$n),] %>% 
  remove_rownames()
origdbmultcancer <- origdbdefcancer %>% 
  subset(origdbdefcancer$Individual_code %in% multpts$Individual_code) %>% 
  distinct()
all(origdbmultcancer$Individual_code %in% multpts$Individual_code) # should be TRUE in console

# add cancer freq status to breakdown which also has no cancer pts
breakdown <- breakdown %>% 
  mutate(cancer_freq_pt_type = dplyr::case_when(Individual_code %in% solepts$Individual_code ~ "sole",
                                                Individual_code %in% multpts$Individual_code ~ "multiple",
                                                Unaffected == TRUE ~ "none",
                                                TRUE ~ "notyet"))

# #save cleaned, breakdown, def, multiple, and sole cancer data as CSV
write_csv(origdbcleaned,
          file = paste0(table_path, "origdbcleaned_germline.csv"))
write_csv(breakdown,
          file = paste0(table_path, "breakdown_germline.csv"))
write_csv(origdbdefcancer,
          file = paste0(table_path, "origdbdefcancer_germline.csv"))
write_csv(origdbsolecancer,
          file = paste0(table_path, "origdbsolecancer_germline.csv"))
write_csv(origdbmultcancer,
          file = paste0(table_path, "origdbmultcancer_germline.csv"))

# cleaning up ATO rescue muts files
# vector from cancer cell 2021 paper doesn't need cleaning
cleaned_mut_rescue_ATO_chen_2021 <- orig_mut_rescue_ATO_chen_2021

cleaned_mut_not_rescue_ATO_chen_2021 <- orig_mut_not_rescue_ATO_chen_2021

# don't really need to clean suppl table either since it only has a few cols of interest which are fine as is
cleaned_mut_rescue_ATO_suppl_song_2023 <- orig_mut_rescue_ATO_suppl_song_2023

# remove other characters in mutant col of website data and left-join with classification from suppl table 
cleaned_mut_rescue_ATO_website_song_2023 <- orig_mut_rescue_ATO_website_song_2023 %>%
  transform(MUTANT = gsub(" \\(.*",
                          "",
                          MUTANT)) %>%
  transform(MUTANT = gsub("p.",
                          "",
                          MUTANT)) %>%
  left_join(.,
            cleaned_mut_rescue_ATO_suppl_song_2023 %>%
              dplyr::select(c(protein_change,
                              mut_classification)),
            by = c("MUTANT" = "protein_change")) %>%
  relocate(mut_classification,
           .after = Summary) %>%
  clean_names()

# compile all muts that can be rescued by ATO, which if present in datasets can be annotated on heatmaps
mut_rescued <- c(cleaned_mut_rescue_ATO_chen_2021,
                 cleaned_mut_rescue_ATO_website_song_2023 %>%
                   subset(transcription_activity_rescuable_by_ato == "Rescuable" & mut_classification %in% c("1",
                                                                                                             "2a")) %>% 
                   pull(mutant)
                 # ,
                 # cleaned_mut_rescue_ATO_suppl_song_2023 %>%
                 #   subset(mut_classification %in% c("1",
                 #                                    "2a")) %>%
                 #   pull(protein_change)
) %>%
  trimws() %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  unique()

# put together ATO muts that are definitely non-rescuable, removing any that happen to be in rescued list
# setdiff(x, y) returns the elements of x that are not in y but asymmetric difference, so setdiff(y, x) gives what elements of y are not in x and could be different answer
mut_not_rescued <- setdiff(c(cleaned_mut_not_rescue_ATO_chen_2021,
                             cleaned_mut_rescue_ATO_website_song_2023 %>%
                               subset(mut_classification %in% c("3")) %>% 
                               pull(mutant)),
                           mut_rescued)

# save rescued mut list to use for somatic analyses too
saveRDS(mut_rescued,
        file = paste0(table_path, 
                      "mut_rescued.rds"))

saveRDS(mut_rescue_PAT,
        file = paste0(table_path, 
                      "mut_rescue_PAT.rds"))

saveRDS(mut_not_rescued,
        file = paste0(table_path, 
                      "mut_not_rescued.rds"))

# output rescued mut list as a csv too
write.csv(mut_rescued[order(parse_number(mut_rescued))] %>% 
            paste0(collapse = ", "),
          file = paste0(table_path,
                        "mut_rescued.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(mut_rescue_PAT[order(parse_number(mut_rescue_PAT))] %>% 
            paste0(collapse = ", "),
          file = paste0(table_path,
                        "mut_rescue_PAT.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(mut_not_rescued[order(parse_number(mut_not_rescued))] %>% 
            paste0(collapse = ", "),
          file = paste0(table_path,
                        "mut_not_rescued.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

$~$

After cleaning the data as above, we are left with 2,231 entries from 1,500 individuals from 1,034 families. Of these 2,231 entries, 2,054 are in patients with cancer (which are 1,325 individuals), while 177 entries are in patients with no cancer at the time of follow-up (which are 175 individuals). Moreover, of these 2,231 entries,

-   674 are in patients with the strict clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni syndrome,

-   366 are in patients with Li-Fraumeni like for the extended clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni,

-   244 are in patients with a family history of cancer which does not fulfill LFS or any of the LFL definitions,

-   170 are in patients with no family history of cancer,

-   78 are in patients with "other" class,

-   434 are in patients classified as TP53_Chompret, and

-   265 are in patients with NA class.

$~$

Furthermore, there are 1,135 entries from 442 individuals with multiple cancers from 403 families. Moreover, of these 1,135 entries,

-   359 are in patients with the strict clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni syndrome,

-   184 are in patients with Li-Fraumeni like for the extended clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni,

-   90 are in patients with a family history of cancer which does not fulfill LFS or any of the LFL definitions,

-   94 are in patients with no family history of cancer,

-   36 are in patients with "other" class,

-   270 are in patients classified as TP53_Chompret, and

-   102 are in patients with NA class.

$~$

On the other hand, there are 919 entries from 883 individuals with only 1 cancer from 699 families. Moreover, of these 919 entries,

-   261 are in patients with the strict clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni syndrome,

-   145 are in patients with Li-Fraumeni like for the extended clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni,

-   127 are in patients with a family history of cancer which does not fulfill LFS or any of the LFL definitions,

-   69 are in patients with no family history of cancer,

-   42 are in patients with "other" class,

-   132 are in patients classified as TP53_Chompret, and

-   143 are in patients with NA class.

# **Select Cancers with Sufficient Data** {#selectcancers}

$~$

Next, I organized cancers by descending tumor ID count and identified cancers with at 100 (or 50, in multiple or sole cancer datasets) distinct tumor IDs which would be used for subsequent analysis, and saved this list of top cancers to a CSV file and as an SVG. This cutoff of 100 (or 50) was chosen to ensure a large enough sample size to confirm any trends in mutations seen later on as meaningful.

$~$


``` r
#count number of distinct mutated tumor IDs by short topology and sort descending
origdbcancersunique <- origdbdefcancer %>%
  group_by(Short_topo) %>%
  summarise(count = n_distinct(Tumor_ID))
origdbcancersunique <- origdbcancersunique[order(-origdbcancersunique$count),] %>%
  remove_rownames()

origdbmultcancersunique <- origdbmultcancer %>%
  group_by(Short_topo) %>%
  summarise(count = n_distinct(Tumor_ID))
origdbmultcancersunique <- origdbmultcancersunique[order(-origdbmultcancersunique$count),] %>%
  remove_rownames()

origdbsolecancersunique <- origdbsolecancer %>%
  group_by(Short_topo) %>%
  summarise(count = n_distinct(Tumor_ID))
origdbsolecancersunique <- origdbsolecancersunique[order(-origdbsolecancersunique$count),] %>%
  remove_rownames()

#keep only short topologies with at least 100 unique mutated tumor IDs and sort descending; likewise for mult and sole cancers but keep with at least 50
origdbcancersover100 <- origdbcancersunique %>%
  subset(count >= 100)
origdbcancersover100 <- origdbcancersover100[order(-origdbcancersover100$count),] %>%
  remove_rownames()

origdbmultcancersover100 <- origdbmultcancersunique %>%
  subset(count >= 50)
origdbmultcancersover100 <- origdbmultcancersover100[order(-origdbmultcancersover100$count),] %>%
  remove_rownames()

origdbsolecancersover100 <- origdbsolecancersunique %>%
  subset(count >= 50)
origdbsolecancersover100 <- origdbsolecancersover100[order(-origdbsolecancersover100$count),] %>%
  remove_rownames()

# define core LFS cancers
core_LFS_tumors <- origdbcancersover100$Short_topo

#add total row at bottom of short topologies with at least 100 unique mutated tumor IDs
origdbcancersover100withtotal <- origdbcancersover100 %>%
  adorn_totals() %>%
  remove_rownames()

origdbmultcancersover100withtotal <- origdbmultcancersover100 %>%
  adorn_totals() %>%
  remove_rownames()

origdbsolecancersover100withtotal <- origdbsolecancersover100 %>%
  adorn_totals() %>%
  remove_rownames()
# 
# #save 100 unique mutated tumor IDs topologies as SVG and CSV
write_csv(origdbcancersover100withtotal,
          file = paste0(table_path, "origdbcancersover100withtotal_germline.csv"))
write_csv(origdbmultcancersover100withtotal,
          file = paste0(table_path, "origdbmultcancersover100withtotal_germline.csv"))
write_csv(origdbsolecancersover100withtotal,
          file = paste0(table_path, "origdbsolecancersover100withtotal_germline.csv"))
# 
# #graph 100 unique mutated tumor IDs topologies as plot
# origdbcancersover100grid <- tableGrob(origdbcancersover100withtotal, 
#                                       rows = NULL, 
#                                       theme = ttheme_default(base_size = 10, 
#                                                              core = list(padding = unit(c(2, 2), "mm"))
#                                       )) 
# origdbcancersgrid <- grid.arrange(origdbcancersover100grid,
#                                   top = textGrob("Distinct samples in all individuals",
#                                                  hjust = 0.485,
#                                                  gp = gpar(fontface = "bold")))
```

$~$

In addition to this list of top 5 cancers, there are 175 individuals with no cancer at the time of follow-up who cumulatively have 177 entries of mutations.

$~$

# **Create Cancer Sequence Table of Individuals with Multiple Cancers** {#cancersequence .hidden .unlisted .unnumbered}

$~$

Since there are 442 patients with at least 2 cancers in their lifetime, I created a cancer sequence table for these patients, similar to Table 2 in @Hisada1998. Thus, I identified the distinct cancers (figuratively collapsing down cancers with duplicate tumor IDs or distinct tumor IDs but same age of diagnosis, same short topology, and same morphology) for each Individual throughout their life and compiled them into a dataframe. I will use this table to make a color-coded map of patients and their cancer landscape over time, as well as stacked barcharts of the proportions of cancers at each incidence (e.g. of all first cancers, what proportion is breast vs. soft tissue vs. other tissue).

$~$



$~$



$~$



$~$

$~$

$~$

Furthermore, there are 448 entries (448 distinct tumor samples) from 442 individuals with multiple cancers from 403 families. Moreover, of these 448 entries,

-   139 are in patients with the strict clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni syndrome,

-   73 are in patients with Li-Fraumeni like for the extended clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni,

-   37 are in patients with a family history of cancer which does not fulfill LFS or any of the LFL definitions,

-   36 are in patients with no family history of cancer,

-   16 are in patients with "other" class,

-   104 are in patients classified as TP53_Chompret, and

-   43 are in patients with NA class.

$~$

On the other hand, there are 919 entries (919 distinct tumor samples) from 883 individuals with 1 cancer from 699 families. Moreover, of these 919 entries,

-   261 are in patients with the strict clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni syndrome,

-   145 are in patients with Li-Fraumeni like for the extended clinical definition of Li-Fraumeni,

-   127 are in patients with a family history of cancer which does not fulfill LFS or any of the LFL definitions,

-   69 are in patients with no family history of cancer,

-   42 are in patients with "other" class,

-   132 are in patients classified as TP53_Chompret, and

-   143 are in patients with NA class.

$~$

# **Create Pivot Tables of Mutation Types and Codons** {#pivottables}

$~$

Now the data, which only includes cancers with at least 100 distinct tumor IDs and anyone without cancer or with no age or sex listed, can be used for data analysis. I created pivot tables of the number of mutation categories and mutated codons per cancer, age stratum, and sex, converted them to dataframes and saved them as CSV files, and have previewed the tables as output below. For the datasets of multiple and sole cancers, as well as a breakdown of cancer types within short topologies, I have counted the number of distinct tumor samples. However, for the full dataset, which also includes patients without cancer, I have to count the number of mutations instead of distinct tumor samples, as the numbers wouldn't properly reflect patients without cancer.

$~$


``` r
# pivot table of cancers by tumor ID, regardless of whether in sole or multiple, to see how many events overall
origdbcancersuniquepivot <- PivotTable$new()
origdbcancersuniquepivot$addData(origdbdefcancer)
origdbcancersuniquepivot$addRowDataGroups("Short_topo")
origdbcancersuniquepivot$defineCalculation(calculationName = "Count of cancers",
                                     summariseExpression = "n_distinct(Tumor_ID)")
origdbcancersuniquepivot$sortColumnDataGroups(levelNumber = 1,
                                        orderBy = "calculation",
                                        sortOrder = "desc")
origdbcancersuniquepivot$sortRowDataGroups(levelNumber = 1,
                                     orderBy = "calculation",
                                     sortOrder = "desc")
origdbcancersuniquepivot$evaluatePivot() #doing this instead of renderPivot() which takes too long as it shows an actual pivot table, but we need this as a dataframe anyways for calculations later so we don't need to print a pivot table
```

``` r
demog_df <- origdbjustsolecancersover100 %>%
  dplyr::select(c(Individual_code,
                  Cancer_Label,
                  Age_stratum,
                  Sex,
                  Region,
                  Class,
                  Mode_of_inheritance,
                  Dead
                  # ,
                  # Domain,
                  # Residue_function,
                  # Effect,
                  # DNE_LOFclass,
                  # SIFTClass,
                  # TransactivationClass
  )) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Inheritance = Mode_of_inheritance) %>%
  mutate(Inheritance = dplyr::case_when(Inheritance == "M" ~ "Maternal",
                                        Inheritance == "P" ~ "Paternal",
                                        Inheritance == "de novo" ~ "De novo",
                                        Inheritance == "de novo, mosaic" ~ "De novo, mosaic",
                                        Inheritance == "NA" ~ "Not listed",
                                        TRUE ~ Inheritance)) %>%
  mutate(Class = gsub("TP53_",
                      "",
                      Class)) %>%
  mutate(Class = dplyr::case_when(Class == "FH" ~ "Family history of cancer",
                                  Class == "noFH" ~ "No family history of cancer",
                                  Class == "NA" ~ "Not listed",
                                  TRUE ~ Class))  %>%
  mutate(Sex = dplyr::case_when(Sex == "M" ~ "Male",
                                Sex == "F" ~ "Female",
                                TRUE ~ Sex)) %>%
  mutate(Cancer_Label = factor(Cancer_Label,
                               levels = c(sort(unique(core_LFS_tumors)),
                                          "OTHER")
  )) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Case = Class,
                `Age stratum of diagnosis` = Age_stratum) %>%
  distinct() 

t <- tbl_summary(demog_df %>%
                   dplyr::select(-c(Individual_code)),
                 by = Cancer_Label,
                 sort = list(everything() ~ "frequency",
                             `Age stratum of diagnosis` ~ "alphanumeric"),
                 missing_text = "Not indicated") %>% 
  bold_labels() %>%
  add_stat_label() %>%
  as_gt()
t
```

``` r
demog_df <- origdbjustmultcancersover100 %>%
  dplyr::select(c(Individual_code,
                  #Cancer_Label,
                  Age_stratum,
                  Sex,
                  Region,
                  Class,
                  Mode_of_inheritance,
                  Dead
                  # ,
                  # Domain,
                  # Residue_function,
                  # Effect,
                  # DNE_LOFclass,
                  # SIFTClass,
                  # TransactivationClass
  )) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Inheritance = Mode_of_inheritance) %>%
  mutate(Inheritance = dplyr::case_when(Inheritance == "M" ~ "Maternal",
                                        Inheritance == "P" ~ "Paternal",
                                        Inheritance == "de novo" ~ "De novo",
                                        Inheritance == "de novo, mosaic" ~ "De novo, mosaic",
                                        Inheritance == "NA" ~ "Not listed",
                                        Inheritance == "M&P" ~ "Maternal and paternal",
                                        TRUE ~ Inheritance)) %>%
  mutate(Class = gsub("TP53_",
                      "",
                      Class)) %>%
  mutate(Class = dplyr::case_when(Class == "FH" ~ "Family history of cancer",
                                  Class == "noFH" ~ "No family history of cancer",
                                  Class == "NA" ~ "Not listed",
                                  TRUE ~ Class))  %>%
  mutate(Sex = dplyr::case_when(Sex == "M" ~ "Male",
                                Sex == "F" ~ "Female",
                                TRUE ~ Sex)) %>%
  # mutate(Cancer_Label = factor(Cancer_Label,
  #                              levels = c(sort(unique(core_LFS_tumors)),
  #                                         "OTHER")
  # )) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Case = Class,
                `Age stratum of diagnosis` = Age_stratum) %>%
  distinct() 

t <- tbl_summary(demog_df %>%
                   dplyr::select(-c(Individual_code)),
                 by = Sex,
                 sort = list(everything() ~ "frequency",
                             `Age stratum of diagnosis` ~ "alphanumeric"),
                 missing_text = "Not indicated") %>% 
  bold_labels() %>%
  add_stat_label() %>%
  as_gt()
t
```

``` r
demog_df <- breakdown %>%
  subset(Unaffected == TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::select(c(Individual_code,
                  #Cancer_Label,
                  Age_stratum,
                  Sex,
                  Region,
                  Class,
                  Mode_of_inheritance,
                  Dead
                  # ,
                  # Domain,
                  # Residue_function,
                  # Effect,
                  # DNE_LOFclass,
                  # SIFTClass,
                  # TransactivationClass
  )) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Inheritance = Mode_of_inheritance) %>%
  mutate(Inheritance = dplyr::case_when(Inheritance == "M" ~ "Maternal",
                                        Inheritance == "P" ~ "Paternal",
                                        Inheritance == "de novo" ~ "De novo",
                                        Inheritance == "de novo, mosaic" ~ "De novo, mosaic",
                                        Inheritance == "NA" ~ "Not listed",
                                        Inheritance == "M&P" ~ "Maternal and paternal",
                                        TRUE ~ Inheritance)) %>%
  mutate(Class = gsub("TP53_",
                      "",
                      Class)) %>%
  mutate(Class = dplyr::case_when(Class == "FH" ~ "Family history of cancer",
                                  Class == "noFH" ~ "No family history of cancer",
                                  Class == "NA" ~ "Not listed",
                                  TRUE ~ Class))  %>%
  mutate(Sex = dplyr::case_when(Sex == "M" ~ "Male",
                                Sex == "F" ~ "Female",
                                TRUE ~ Sex)) %>%
  # mutate(Cancer_Label = factor(Cancer_Label,
  #                              levels = c(sort(unique(core_LFS_tumors)),
  #                                         "OTHER")
  # )) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Case = Class,
                `Age stratum of last follow-up` = Age_stratum
                ) %>%
  distinct() 

t <- tbl_summary(demog_df %>%
                   dplyr::select(-c(Individual_code)),
                 by = Sex,
                 sort = list(everything() ~ "frequency",
                             `Age stratum of last follow-up` ~ "alphanumeric"
                             ),
                 missing_text = "Not indicated") %>% 
  bold_labels() %>%
  add_stat_label() %>%
  as_gt()
t
```

# **Calculating Proportions of Mutation Types and Positions** {#calcproportions}

$~$

Now that I have the counts of mutation types or positions per cancer, age, and sex, I calculated the proportions across all cancers, ages, and sexes for each dataset, i.e. the number of mutations divided by the total number of mutations. I also saved these calculated results as CSV files, expressly labeled entries from patients without cancer or with no ages listed as such (so that figures are appropriately labeled), and subsetted the datasets to only include mutated codons with at least a 1% proportion as well as removing mutations with no ages listed (since our analysis is expressly concerned with listed ages and mutations in age brackets). As the saved CSV files do not have this 1% threshold or non-cancer/non-age labeling, they can be edited later on as needed for other types of analysis. I have displayed a preview of the datasets below.

A 1% proportion threshold was chosen to select for mutations present at relatively substantial levels, as including all mutated residues would lead to an illegible heatmap with hundreds of columns of alterations. Subsequent analysis can indeed include all mutated residues if desired, or impose a different percent threshold, simply by changing the code below and the input data for clustered heatmap generation towards the end. Of note, only the specific mutated codon datasets were subsetted at a 1% proportion threshold; the mutation category datasets have not undergone any threshold cutoff.

$~$


``` r

defcancersuniquepivot_calc <- defcancersuniquepivot %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Total = `Count of cancers`) %>% 
  transform(Short_topo = paste0(Short_topo,
                                " (",
                                format(Total, 
                                      big.mark = ",", 
                                      trim = TRUE),
                                " events)")) %>%
  transform(Short_topo = ifelse(Total == 1,
                                gsub("events",
                                     "event",
                                     Short_topo),
                                Short_topo)) %>% 
  mutate(prop = Total/last(Total)) %>% 
  remove_rownames()

multcancerpivottypenobottom <- multcancerpivottype %>% 
  subset(Short_topo != "Total") %>% 
  transform(Short_topo = paste0(Short_topo,
                                " (",
                                Total,
                                " individuals)")) %>%
  transform(Short_topo = ifelse(Total == 1,
                                gsub("individuals",
                                     "individual",
                                     Short_topo),
                                Short_topo)) %>%
  remove_rownames()

colnames(multcancerpivottypenobottom) <- colnames(multcancerpivottype)

multcancerpivotposnobottom <- multcancerpivotpos %>%
```

``` r
# vectors for pie chart of how most muts are chosen anyways for heatmap
prop <- n_distinct(solecancerpivotpos_melted_over0.01 %>% 
                     drop_na(Proportion) %>% 
                     pull(Mutation) %>%
                     as.vector()) / n_distinct(solecancerpivotpos_melted %>% 
                                                 drop_na(Proportion) %>% 
                                                 pull(Mutation) %>%
                                                 as.vector())
vec <- c(prop,
         1 - prop)
raw <- c(n_distinct(solecancerpivotpos_melted_over0.01 %>% 
                      drop_na(Proportion) %>% 
                      pull(Mutation) %>%
                      as.vector()),
         n_distinct(setdiff(unique(solecancerpivotpos_melted %>% 
                                     drop_na(Proportion) %>% 
                                     pull(Mutation) %>%
                                     as.vector()),
                            unique(solecancerpivotpos_melted_over0.01 %>% 
                                     drop_na(Proportion) %>% 
                                     pull(Mutation) %>%
                                     as.vector()))))

# make prevalence waterfall plots (base R barplots + abline at 1%) of all muts in solecancer to justify why 1% chosen for cutting off
barplot(height = sort(as.numeric(solecancerpivotpos_melted$Proportion) %>% na.omit(),
                      decreasing = TRUE),
        xaxs = "i", # remove space between left side of bars and y axis
        ylab = "Proportion of distinct individuals with cancer", 
        xlab = "p53 mutation",
        main = "Prevalence of p53 Mutations in Distinct Individuals with Cancer",
        font.lab = 2,
        ylim = c(0, plyr::round_any(max(solecancerpivotpos_melted$Proportion,
                                        na.rm = TRUE),
                                    0.1,
                                    f = ceiling)),
        col = ifelse((solecancerpivotpos_melted %>% 
                        #drop_na(Proportion) %>% 
                        pull(Mutation) %>%
                        as.vector()) %in% (solecancerpivotpos_melted_over0.01 %>% 
                                             #drop_na(Proportion) %>% 
                                             pull(Mutation) %>%
                                             as.vector()),
                     "black",
                     "grey"),
        las = 1,
        space = 0,
        border = NA)
abline(h = 0.01,
       col = "red",
       lty = 2,
       lwd = 2)
legend("right",
       legend = c("Subset", 
                  "Other"),
       col = c("black", 
               "gray"),
       bty = "n", # no border around legend
       pch = 15, # filled square shape
       pt.cex = 1.75) # increase shape size in legend
```

``` r
# divide down to calc prop of muts in all sole pts, add as new col and mult by 100, remove codon 0 which is intronic muts throughout p53, remove total row, and sort by increasing codon
codon_barplot_df <- solepivotcodon %>%
  mutate(Prop = `Count of distinct patients`/last(`Count of distinct patients`)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Count_of_distinct_patients = `Count of distinct patients`) %>%
  mutate(Prop_Label = plyr::round_any(Prop * 100,
                                      0.1)) %>%
  subset(!(Codon_number %in% c("0",
                               "Total"))) %>%
  mutate_at("Codon_number",
            as.numeric) %>%
  arrange(Codon_number)

# because not all codons mutated need to add in missing codons as 0 pts and 0 prop
missing_codons <- data.frame(Codon_number = setdiff(1:393, # since p53 has 393 codons
                                                    codon_barplot_df$Codon_number),
                             Count_of_distinct_patients = 0,
                             Prop = 0,
                             Prop_Label = 0)

# add missing codons to df
codon_barplot_df <- full_join(codon_barplot_df,
                              missing_codons) %>%
  arrange(Codon_number)

# barplot, adding codon numbers at intervals and label numbers of codons >= 1.5%
barplot(height = codon_barplot_df$Prop,
        xaxs = "i", # remove space between left side of bars and y axis
        ylab = "Proportion of distinct individuals with cancer", 
        xlab = "Codon",
        main = "Prevalence of p53 Mutations in Distinct Individuals with Cancer",
        #axis.lty = 1,
        #names.arg = codon_barplot_df$Codon_number,
        ylim = c(0, plyr::round_any(max(codon_barplot_df$Prop, 
                                        na.rm = TRUE), 
                                    0.1, 
                                    f = ceiling)),
        font.lab = 2,
        col = dplyr::case_when(codon_barplot_df$Prop >= 0.02 & codon_barplot_df$Codon_number %in% c(175,
                                                                                                    213, 
                                                                                                    245, 
                                                                                                    248, 
                                                                                                    273,
```

$~$

Furthermore, with this 1% proportion cutoff, there are 109 distinct alterations across the 5 cancers in patients with 2 or more cancers. This cutoff marks a substantial reduction in datapoints to facilitate clustered heatmap generation, as the full dataset before the 1% proportion cutoff has 182 distinct alterations across the 5 cancers.

$~$

On the other hand, with this 1% proportion cutoff, there are 95 distinct alterations across the 5 cancers in patients with 1 cancer. This cutoff marks a substantial reduction in datapoints to facilitate clustered heatmap generation, as the full dataset before the 1% proportion cutoff has 270 distinct alterations across the 5 cancers.

$~$



$~$

$~$

When age is considered, after the 1% proportion cutoff, there are 116 distinct alterations in patients with 2 or more cancers across the 5 age strata. This cutoff again marks a substantial reduction in datapoints to facilitate clustered heatmap generation, as the full dataset before the 1% proportion cutoff has 182 distinct alterations across the 5 age strata.

$~$

When age is considered, after the 1% proportion cutoff, there are 62 distinct alterations in patients with 1 cancer across the 5 age strata. This cutoff again marks a substantial reduction in datapoints to facilitate clustered heatmap generation, as the full dataset before the 1% proportion cutoff has 270 distinct alterations across the 5 age strata.

$~$



$~$

$~$

When sex is considered, after the 1% proportion cutoff, there are 33 distinct alterations in patients with 2 or more cancers. This cutoff again marks a substantial reduction in datapoints to facilitate clustered heatmap generation, as the full dataset before the 1% proportion cutoff has 182 distinct alterations.

$~$

When sex is considered, after the 1% proportion cutoff, there are 24 distinct alterations in patients with 1 cancer. This cutoff again marks a substantial reduction in datapoints to facilitate clustered heatmap generation, as the full dataset before the 1% proportion cutoff has 270 distinct alterations.

$~$

# **Creating Annotations for Heatmaps** {#annotations}

$~$

Next, I have to prepare annotations for the clustered heatmaps I plan to create for these proportions. Here I am preparing to have mutated codons ordered numerically and by p53 domain. Although the domains were partially annotated in the original dataset, for consistency and complete information I have defined the p53 domains as per a few previously published papers [@joruiz2020; @cho1994]. Moreover, I am assigning germ layers to cancers to make it an annotation as well. I also formatted the annotations object to have cancers/no cancer and mutated positions as rownames as this setup is required for the ComplexHeatmap package I will be using.

$~$

``` r
  transform(Germ_Layer = ifelse(Cancer_temp %in% c("LUNG",

  dplyr::select(-Cancer_temp)
```

``` r
unique(solecancermutinfo_annotate_sex$Domain) #to find list of domains in order to use as factors

                                                levels = c("DBD",

                                                           "DBD L3 loop", 
                                                           "HD", 
                                                           "OD",
                                                           "NA"))

sort(as.vector(unique(solecancermutinfo_annotate_sex$Residue_function))) #to find list of residue functions in order to use as factors

                                                          levels = c("Buried", 
                                                                     "DNA binding", 
                                                                     "Exposed", 
                                                                     "Partially exposed", 
                                                                     "Tetramerisation/Methylation site", 
                                                                     "NA"))

solecancermutinfo_annotate_sex$Rescuable <- factor(solecancermutinfo_annotate_sex$Rescuable, 
                                                 levels = sort(as.vector(unique(solecancermutinfo_annotate_sex$Rescuable)),

solecancermutinfo_annotate_sex$SIFTClass <- factor(solecancermutinfo_annotate_sex$SIFTClass,

                                                              "NA"))

solecancermutinfo_annotate_sex$DNE_LOFclass <- factor(solecancermutinfo_annotate_sex$DNE_LOFclass,
                                                      levels = c("DNE_LOF",

                                                                 "notDNE_notLOF",
                                                                 "unclass.",
                                                                 "NA"))
```

``` r
mut_rescued_hematological_gridprep <- condformat(origdbjustsolecancersover100 %>% 
                                                   subset(Short_topo == "HEMATOP. SYSTEM") %>%
                                                   mutate(Sex = dplyr::case_when(Sex == "M" ~ "Male",
                                                                                 Sex == "F" ~ "Female",
                                                                                 TRUE ~ Sex)) %>% 
                                                   dplyr::select(c(Short_topo,
                                                                   Morphology,
                                                                   #Population, 
                                                                   #Region,
                                                                   Sex,
                                                                   Age_stratum,
                                                                   Effect,
                                                                   ProtDescription,
                                                                   Domain,
                                                                   Residue_function,
                                                                   SIFTClass,
                                                                   DNE_LOFclass)) %>% 
                                                   arrange(abs(parse_number(ProtDescription))) %>% 
                                                   arrange(Morphology) %>% 
                                                   # mutate(ProtDescription = gsub("\\?-0-splice",
                                                   #                               "Intronic",
                                                   #                               ProtDescription)) %>% 
                                                   # mutate(ProtDescription = gsub("\\?",
                                                   #                               "",
                                                   #                               ProtDescription)) %>%
                                                   mutate(across(everything(), 
                                                                 ~ replace(., 
                                                                           . %in% c("NA", NA),
                                                                           ""))) %>% 
                                                   dplyr::rename(System = Short_topo,
                                                                 Cancer = Morphology,
                                                                 `Age stratum` = Age_stratum,
                                                                 Type = Effect,
                                                                 Mutation = ProtDescription,
                                                                 `Feature` = Residue_function,
                                                                 `SIFT` = SIFTClass,
                                                                 `DNE` = DNE_LOFclass) %>% 
                                                   remove_rownames()) %>% 
  rule_text_color(Mutation,
                  ifelse(Mutation %in% mut_rescued,
                         "red",
                         "")) %>%
  rule_text_bold(Mutation,
                 expression = Mutation %in% mut_rescued) %>%
  theme_grob(rows = NULL, 
             theme = ttheme_default(base_size = 10,
                                    core = list(padding = unit(c(15, 4), "mm")))) %>%
  condformat2grob(draw = FALSE)

mut_rescued_hematological_grid <- grid.arrange(mut_rescued_hematological_gridprep,
                                               top = textGrob("Individuals with Hematological Cancers and Germline TP53 Mutations",
                                                              hjust = 0.5,
                                                              gp = gpar(fontface = "bold"))) 
```

<img src="figures/mut-rescued-hematological-grid-1.svg" alt="" width="100%" height="100%" style="display: block; margin: auto;" />

``` r
soleotherpivotage_gridprep <- condformat(soleotherpivotage %>%
                                           mutate(across(everything(), 
                                                         ~ replace(., 
                                                                   . %in% c("NA", NA),
                                                                   ""))) %>%
                                           relocate(colnames(.)[c(6,4,5,3,2)], # make ages ascending 
                                                    .after = Short_topo) %>%
                                           dplyr::rename(System = Short_topo) %>%
                                           remove_rownames()) %>%
  rule_text_bold(Total,
                 expression = Total > 0) %>%
  # rule_fill_discrete(Total,
  #                    expression = Total > 0,
  #                    colours = c("TRUE" = "grey80")) %>% # also adds unremovable black borders
  theme_grob(rows = NULL, 
             theme = ttheme_default(base_size = 10,
                                    core = list(padding = unit(c(15, 4), "mm"),
                                                fg_params = list(fontface = c(rep("plain", 
                                                                                  nrow(soleotherpivotage) - 1), 
                                                                              "bold")),
                                                bg_params = list(fill = c(rep(c("grey95", "grey90"),
                                                                              length.out = (nrow(soleotherpivotage) - 1)),
                                                                          "grey80")))
             )) %>%
  condformat2grob(draw = FALSE)
```

# **Drawing Cancer Breakdown Stacked Barcharts** {#breakdownbarcharts .hidden .unlisted .unnumbered}

$~$

Now that the samples per cancers data has been set up in a table, I can create stacked barcharts of the breakdown of cancers in the tissue types which require this breakdown, i.e. breast, brain, and soft tissues. As they did not have enough specific detailed cancer types, a breakdown would give a representation of the cancers used in the above calculations and subsequent plots.

$~$



$~$



$~$



$~$



$~$



$~$



$~$



$~$



$~$



$~$



$~$



$~$



$~$



$~$

# **Drawing 100% Stacked Barcharts** {#barcharts}

$~$

Now that proportions have been calculated, I can visualize them with a few types of plots. Here, I have created 100% stacked barcharts of mutation categories across the 5 cancers or in those without cancer, ages, and sexes, and have saved the plots as SVG files.

$~$

``` r
#sort cancers by lowest to highest missense mutation or breast proportion for stacked barchart
solecancerbarchartorder = solecancerpivottype_melted[solecancerpivottype_melted$Mutation == 'missense',]
solecancerpivottype_melted$Cancer_Label = factor(solecancerpivottype_melted$Cancer_Label, 
                                                 levels = solecancerbarchartorder$Cancer_Label[order(solecancerbarchartorder$Proportion)])

solecancerbarchartorder_age = solecancerpivotage_type_melted[solecancerpivotage_type_melted$Mutation == 'missense',]
solecancerpivotage_type_melted$Age = factor(solecancerpivotage_type_melted$Age, 
                                            levels = solecancerbarchartorder_age$Age[order(solecancerbarchartorder_age$Proportion)])

# solecancerbarchartorder_age_tissue = solecancerpivotage_melted[solecancerpivotage_melted$Cancer_Label == 'BREAST',]
# solecancerpivotage_melted$Age = factor(solecancerpivotage_melted$Age, 
#                                        levels = solecancerbarchartorder_age_tissue$Age[order(solecancerbarchartorder_age_tissue$Proportion)])

solecancerpivotage_melted$Cancer_Label <- factor(solecancerpivotage_melted$Cancer_Label,
                                                 levels = as.character(c((sort(unique(solecancerpivotage_melted$Cancer_Label)))[(sort(unique(solecancerpivotage_melted$Cancer_Label))) != "OTHER"], 
                                                                         "OTHER")))

solecancerbarchartorder_sex = solecancerpivotsex_type_melted[solecancerpivotsex_type_melted$Mutation == 'missense',]
solecancerpivotsex_type_melted$Sex = factor(solecancerpivotsex_type_melted$Sex, 
                                            levels = solecancerbarchartorder_sex$Sex[order(solecancerbarchartorder_sex$Proportion)])

# solecancerbarchartorder_sex_tissue = solecancerpivotsex_melted[solecancerpivotsex_melted$Cancer_Label == 'BREAST',]
# solecancerpivotsex_melted$Sex = factor(solecancerpivotsex_melted$Sex, 
#                                        levels = solecancerbarchartorder_sex_tissue$Sex[order(solecancerbarchartorder_sex_tissue$Proportion)])

solecancerpivotsex_melted$Cancer_Label <- factor(solecancerpivotsex_melted$Cancer_Label,
                                                 levels = as.character(c((sort(unique(solecancerpivotsex_melted$Cancer_Label)))[(sort(unique(solecancerpivotsex_melted$Cancer_Label))) != "OTHER"], 
                                                                         "OTHER")))

# make 100% stacked barchart with ggplot2 with reversed missense order i.e. highest to lowest
solecancer_ggplotstackedbarchart <- ggplot(solecancerpivottype_melted %>%
                                             subset(!str_detect(Cancer_Label,
                                                                "OTHER")), 
                                           aes(x = Cancer_Label, 
                                               y = Proportion, 
                                               fill = Mutation)) + 
  geom_bar(position = "fill", 
           stat = "identity") + 
  ggtitle("Mutation Types vs. Cancers of \nIndividuals with One Cancer \nand Germline p53 Mutations") + # distinct individuals/ \n# total distinct individuals
  xlab("Cancer") +
  ylab("Proportion of distinct individuals") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(), 
                     expand = c(0,0), 
                     breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 6)) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = rev(levels(solecancerpivottype_melted$Cancer_Label)[!str_detect(levels(solecancerpivottype_melted$Cancer_Label), 
                                                                                            "OTHER")]), 
                   expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#009E73",
                               "#000000",
                               "#0072B2",
                               "#CC79A7",
                               "#999999",
                               "#E69F00",
                               "lightgray",
                               "#56B4E9",
                               "#D55E00",
                               "#F0E442")) +   
  theme_classic() + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, 
                                   hjust = 1, 
                                   vjust = 1), 
        axis.text = element_text(color = "black",
                                 size = 12), 
        axis.title = element_text(color = "black",
                                  face = "bold",
                                  size = 14),
        axis.title.x = element_text(margin = unit(c(5,0,0,0), units = "mm")),
        axis.title.y = element_text(margin = unit(c(0,5,0,0), units = "mm")),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5,
                                  face = "bold",
                                  color = "black",
                                  size = 16,
                                  margin = margin(0,0,5,0, "mm")),
        # plot.title.position = "plot",
        legend.text = element_text(color = "black",
                                   size = 12),
        legend.title = element_text(color = "black",
                                    face = "bold",
                                    size = 14),
        plot.margin = margin(0,0,0,8, "mm"))
solecancer_ggplotstackedbarchart
```

``` r
# to minimize above crowding, make faceted barchart of age vs number of pts per cancer
barchart_facet_age_tissue_sole <- ggplot(solecancerpivotage %>%
                                           subset(Age_stratum != "Total") %>%
                                           mutate(Age_stratum = paste0(Age_stratum,
                                                                       " (",
                                                                       format(Total, 
                                                                              big.mark = ",", 
                                                                              trim = TRUE),
                                                                       " individuals)")) %>%
                                           dplyr::select(-c(Total
                                                            #,
                                                            #OTHER
                                           )) %>% 
                                           mutate(across(everything(), 
                                                         ~ replace_na(.x, 0))) %>%
                                           reshape2::melt() %>% 
                                           dplyr::rename(Age = Age_stratum,
                                                         Cancer = variable, 
                                                         Num_Distinct_Pts = value),
                                         aes(x = factor(Cancer,
                                                        levels = 
                                                          c(
                                                            sort(unique(colnames(solecancerpivotage %>% 
                                                                                   dplyr::select(-c(
                                                                                     OTHER,
                                                                                     Total, 
                                                                                     Age_stratum)))))
                                                            ,
                                                            "OTHER")
                                         ),
                                         y = Num_Distinct_Pts,
                                         fill = factor(Cancer,
                                                       levels = 
                                                         c(
                                                           sort(unique(colnames(solecancerpivotage %>% 
                                                                                  dplyr::select(-c(
                                                                                    OTHER,
                                                                                    Total, 
                                                                                    Age_stratum)))))
                                                           ,
                                                           "OTHER")
                                         ))) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", 
           position = position_dodge2()) + # to keep some space b/t barcharts in same mut
  geom_text(aes(label = Num_Distinct_Pts,
                vjust = -1),
            color = "black",
            fontface = "bold",
            size = 3.5,
            alpha = 0.5) + # add num pts above each bar
  ggtitle("Cancers vs. Ages of Cancer Diagnoses in Individuals with Germline p53 Mutations") +
  xlab("Cancer") +
  ylab("Number of distinct individuals") +
  labs(fill = "Cancer") +
  facet_wrap2(. ~ Age,
              #strip.position = "right",
              #labeller = labeller(groupwrap = label_wrap_gen(10)), # wrap labels on right based on characters
              ncol = 3,
              axes = "all", # show internal axes but without x labels
              remove_labels = "x") + # show internal axes but without x labels
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) + 
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)
                     #,
                     #n.breaks = 7
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, (solecancerpivotage %>%
                                 subset(Age_stratum != "Total") %>%
                                 dplyr::select(-c(Total
                                                  #,
                                                  #OTHER
                                 )) %>%
                                 reshape2::melt() %>%
                                 pull(value) %>%
                                 na.omit() %>%
                                 max() %>%
                                 plyr::round_any(50,
                                                 ceiling)))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#CC79A7",
                               "#E69F00",
                               "#009E73",
                               "#56B4E9",
                               "#999999"
                               ,
                               "#000000"
                               #,
                               #"#F0E442",
                               #"#0072B2",
                               #"#D55E00"
  )) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, 
                                   hjust = 1, 
                                   vjust = 1), 
        axis.text = element_text(color = "black",
                                 size = 12), 
        axis.title = element_text(color = "black",
                                  face = "bold",
                                  size = 14),
        axis.title.x = element_text(margin = unit(c(10,0,0,0), units = "mm")),
        axis.title.y = element_text(margin = unit(c(0,10,0,0), units = "mm")),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5,
                                  face = "bold",
                                  color = "black",
                                  size = 16,
                                  margin = margin(0,0,10,0, "mm")),
        legend.text = element_text(color = "black",
                                   size = 12),
        legend.title = element_text(color = "black",
                                    face = "bold",
                                    size = 14),
        legend.box.spacing = margin(30), # increase space between legend and plot
        legend.position = c(0.97, 0.1), # make legend occupy bottom right empty space
        legend.justification = c(0.97, 0), # make legend occupy bottom right empty space
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(color = "black",
                                  size = 14,
                                  face = "bold",
                                  margin = margin(0,0,5,0, "mm")),
        panel.spacing.y = unit(-4, "lines"),
        panel.spacing.x = unit(2.8, "lines"),
        plot.margin = margin(0,2,0,10, unit = "mm"))
```

# **Drawing Plots to Justify Cutoffs** {#justifyplots}

$~$

$~$


``` r
# proportion of how 40+ pts cutoff captures most pts with p53 muts
solepropor_over40muts <- (solecancerpivottype %>%
                            subset(Short_topo %in% origdbcancersover100$Short_topo) %>%
                            pull(Total) %>%
                            sum()) / n_distinct(origdbsolecancer$Individual_code)

zed <- origdbsolecancer %>%
  group_by(Short_topo) %>%
  summarise(n = n_distinct(Individual_code)) %>%
  arrange(-n)

vec <- c(solepropor_over40muts,
         1 - solepropor_over40muts)

raw <- c(solecancerpivottype %>%
           subset(Short_topo %in% origdbcancersover100$Short_topo) %>%
           pull(Total) %>%
           sum(),
         solecancerpivottype %>%
           subset(Short_topo == "OTHER") %>%
           pull(Total))

barplot(height = sort(as.numeric(zed$n),
                      decreasing = TRUE),
        xaxs = "i", # remove space between left side of bars and y axis
        ylab = "Number of distinct individuals", 
        xlab = "Cancer",
        main = "Prevalence of Distinct Individuals with p53-Mutant Cancers",
        ylim = c(0, plyr::round_any(max(as.numeric(zed$n)),
                                    10, 
                                    f = ceiling)),
        col = ifelse(zed$Short_topo %in% origdbcancersover100$Short_topo,
                     "black",
                     "grey"),
        font.lab = 2,
        las = 1,
        space = 0,
        border = NA) 
abline(h = 40,
       col = "red",
       lty = 2,
       lwd = 2)
legend("right",
       legend = c("Subset", 
                  "Other"),
       col = c("black", 
               "gray"),
       bty = "n", # no border around legend
       pch = 15, # filled square shape
       pt.cex = 1.75) # increase shape size in legend
```

``` r
# make df of prevalence of cancers in entire sole dataset
df_prev <- zed %>%
  adorn_totals() %>%
  mutate(prop = n/last(n)) %>% 
  subset(Short_topo != "Total") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Cancer = Short_topo) %>% 
  mutate(Cancer_Label = paste0(Cancer,
                               " (",
                               format(n, 
                                      big.mark = ",", 
                                      trim = TRUE),
                               " individuals)")) %>% 
  mutate(Cancer_Label = ifelse(n == 1,
                               gsub("individuals",
                                    "individual",
                                    Cancer_Label),
                               Cancer_Label)) %>% 
  mutate(coloring = ifelse(Cancer %in% core_LFS_tumors,
                           "subset",
                           "cancer"))

# make barchart
justify_sole_cancer_prevalence_barchart <- ggplot(df_prev,
                                                  aes(x = factor(Cancer_Label,
                                                                 levels = unique(df_prev$Cancer_Label)),
                                                      y = prop,
                                                      fill = relevel(as.factor(coloring),
                                                                     ref = "subset"))) + 
  geom_bar(position = position_dodge2(), 
           stat = "identity") + 
  ggtitle("Proportion of Cancers in Individuals with Germline Mutations in TP53") + 
  xlab("Cancer") +
  ylab("Proportion of distinct individuals") +
  labs(fill = "Type") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(), 
                     expand = c(0,0), 
                     breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 5),
                     limits = c(0, plyr::round_any(max(df_prev$prop),
                                                   0.1,
                                                   f = ceiling) * 1.0000001)) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#0072B2",
                               "skyblue")) +
  theme_classic() + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, 
                                   hjust = 1, 
                                   vjust = 1), 
        axis.text = element_text(color = "black",
                                 size = 12), 
        axis.title = element_text(color = "black",
                                  face = "bold",
                                  size = 14),
        axis.title.x = element_text(margin = unit(c(10,0,0,0), units = "mm")),
        axis.title.y = element_text(margin = unit(c(0,10,0,0), units = "mm")),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5,
                                  face = "bold",
                                  color = "black",
```

# **Drawing Clustered Heatmaps** {#heatmaps}

$~$

Next, I drew clustered heatmaps for mutation types and positions vs. cancers or no cancer, ages, or sexes. In all cases I have at least clustered cancers and ages, while I have also clustered mutation categories when depicted. I have not clustered mutated positions to preserve numeric order and p53 domains, and they would cluster at hotspots first anyways followed by more dispersed arrangements.

``` r
# see if age, sex, cancer, or other variables could explain different mutational profiles seen in heatmaps
# to do this, need multivariate analysis incorporating these variables into GLM to see what is independently associated with mutations

# first need hierarchical clustering of mutations scaled data in heatmap to identify clusters
solecancerpos_hclust <- stats::hclust(dist(scale(t(solecancerpos_matrix_ordered)), # for muts as rows
                                           method = "euclidean"),
                                      method = "complete")
plot(as.dendrogram(solecancerpos_hclust),
     ylim = c(0, plyr::round_any(max(solecancerpos_hclust$height), 1, f = ceiling)))
height_to_cut <- 6.2
abline(h = height_to_cut,
       col = "red",
       lty = 2,
       lwd = 2)
```

<img src="figures/multivariateGLM-1.svg" alt="" width="100%" height="100%" style="display: block; margin: auto;" />

``` r
solecancerpos_clusters <- stats::cutree(solecancerpos_hclust, 
                                        h = height_to_cut) # height to cut at for the clusters you visually think are best, if want to define number of clusters do k = # but bear in mind this is based on the clusters achieved from uniform height, not what you think the end result clusters are at the bottom

# color code clusters and add cluster group numbers to dendrogram
clust_cutree <- dendextend:::cutree(as.dendrogram(solecancerpos_hclust), 
                                    k = max(solecancerpos_clusters), 
                                    order_clusters_as_data = FALSE)
idx <- order(names(clust_cutree))
clust_cutree <- clust_cutree[idx]
df_merge <- merge(solecancerpos_clusters,
                  clust_cutree,
                  by = 'row.names')
df_merge_sorted <- df_merge[order(df_merge$y),]
lbls <- unique(df_merge_sorted$x)
plot(dendextend::color_branches(as.dendrogram(solecancerpos_hclust) %>% 
                                  dendextend::set("labels_cex", 
                                                  1.1) %>%
                                  dendextend::set("labels_col",
                                                  k = length(lbls)) %>%
                                  dendextend::set("branches_lwd",
                                                  2),  
                                k = max(solecancerpos_clusters), 
                                groupLabels = lbls,
                                cex = 10),
     ylim = c(0, plyr::round_any(max(solecancerpos_hclust$height), 1, f = ceiling)))
```

``` r
# check that all muts in orig df are accounted for in heatmap matrix that led to clustering, because if not then won't have cluster information for those individuals
ncol(solecancerpos_matrix_ordered) == n_distinct(origdbjustsolecancersover100$ProtDescription) # not true


# add cluster numbers to orig df
origdbjustsolecancersover100_forGLM <- left_join(origdbjustsolecancersover100,

                                                 by = "ProtDescription")




# for binomial glm convert all categorical variables to factors and binarize dependent response variable, and make reference level the opposite of what you want to predict so that is the baseline to compare regression on 
origdbjustsolecancersover100_forGLM <- origdbjustsolecancersover100_forGLM %>%
  transform(Age_stratum_binary = ifelse(Age_stratum %in% c("0-9",
                                                           "10-19"),
                                        "Younger than 20",
                                        "20 and up")) %>%
  transform(Cancer_Label_binary = ifelse(Cancer_Label %in% c("OTHER"),
                                         "OTHER",

  transform(Effect_binary = ifelse(Effect %in% c("missense"),
                                   "missense",

  mutate_at(c(#'Age_vs_mut_cluster',
              #'Sex_vs_mut_cluster',
              'Cancer_vs_mut_cluster',
              'Age_stratum',
              'Age_stratum_binary',
              'Effect',

              'CpG_site',

            as.factor)

origdbjustsolecancersover100_forGLM$Region <- relevel(origdbjustsolecancersover100_forGLM$Region,
```

``` r
# #        lty = 2,
# #        lwd = 2)
# abline(h = 0.75, # Jaccard >= 0.75 is valid and stable cluster
#        col = "forestgreen",
#        lty = 2,
#        lwd = 2)

# calc jaccard similarity for all 1:ideal clusters' stabilities
bootres_all <- lapply(1:5 # 5 close enough to ideal
                      #as.numeric(silhouette_solecancerpos$data$clusters[which.max(silhouette_solecancerpos$data$y)])
                      ,
                      FUN = function(x) clusterboot(scale(t(solecancerpos_matrix_ordered)), 
                                                    clustermethod = hclustCBI,
                                                    scaling = FALSE, # data already provided as scaled so don't need to rescale
                                                    method = "complete", 
                                                    k = x, 
                                                    seed = 1212,
                                                    count = FALSE))

# plot all cluster numbers' jaccard barplots with lines indicating stable clusters
lapply(1:length(bootres_all),
       FUN = function(x) {barplot(bootres_all[[x]][["bootmean"]], 
                                  xaxs = "i", # remove space between left side of bars and y axis
                                  ylim = c(0, 1),
                                  names.arg = c(1:x),
                                  main = "Cluster stability",
                                  xlab = "Cluster", 
                                  ylab = "Jaccard similarity",
                                  col = ifelse(bootres_all[[x]][["bootmean"]] < 0.6, # Jaccard < 0.6 is unstable cluster, shouldn't be trusted
                                               "red",
                                               "gray"),
                                  font.lab = 2,
                                  las = 1)
         abline(h = 0.75, # Jaccard >= 0.75 is valid and stable cluster
                col = "forestgreen",
                lty = 2,
                lwd = 2)})
```
